messages:
sanjay: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a tiny "soft-preference" layer that sits above the existing policy graph. goal: bias routing toward preferred regions/tiers without triggering hard rejections when capacity/cost changes. thoughts?

mara: can you sketch the contract? is this local to the runtime or in the policy service?

sanjay: idea: policy graph emits candidate routes + hard constraints. then a lightweight preference evaluator adjusts scores with small additive/subtractive penalties. runtime applies thresholding only for hard constraints. preference layer only changes order, never drops compatibility.

liz: so it’s essentially a scoring shim. how do we keep it deterministic across replicas? we already saw route-flapping when weights differed.

sanjay: good call. deterministic seed + stable normalization per-request. preferences must be derived from tenant config (immutable per rollout) or from a global experiment flag. no per-node randomness.

kevin: what about interaction with capacity shims / preemptive slots? if pref biases toward region A, but region A is near capacity and uses preemptive slots, we could increase latency/cost unexpectedly. need a guard.

sanjay: plan: add a guard that queries the existing capacity hint API (cheap probe) and downweights pref if capacity < X. fallback still allowed. prefering region shouldn't override strong capacity signals.

mara: telemetry hooks? ops will want to see pref hit-rate and when the guard trimmed it.

sanjay: yes — emit metrics: pref_applied:boolean, pref_delta:float, pref_overridden:boolean, pref_target_region:string. add trace tag for the policy chain position.

opsbot: deploybot: lint ok, small follow-up: add canary rollout with 5% traffic for 48h. Alert if median latency delta > 5% or cost/unit > 7%.

liz: rollout sounds fine. one more: how do we express preferences in DSL? example snippet:

```
preference {
  name: "region_bias_eu",
  targets: ["eu-west-1", "eu-central-1"],
  weight: 0.15, # additive on normalized score
  max_penalty_override: 0.5, # cap on how much pref can move score
  disable_when_capacity_below: 0.2
}
```

kevin: small nit: prefer weight in [-1,1] so it can prefer or disprefer. also add ttl for ephemeral experiments.

sanjay: agreed. will change to signed weight and add ttl. also add a rollout plan: config flag behind ff, 5/20/50 canary stages, telemetry checks from opsbot, then 100% if green.

mara: ops checklist: add dashboards for pref_overridden ratio, pref_delta distribution, and a heatmap of target_region vs actual_region chosen. Also add a postmortem playbook entry in case prefs introduce oscillation.

sanjay: action items: 1) I’ll draft a short RFC patch with DSL + runtime contract (due EOD Thu). 2) @kevin will prototype the guard logic and capacity call (PR next week). 3) @liz will own determinism tests for cross-replica parity. 4) @mara will spec telemetry dashboards.

kevin: 👍 I’ll ping infra about adding a cheap capacity hint endpoint if we need it.

liz: lgtm. keep the pref logic pure scoring — no hard rejections. small, observable iteration.

sanjay: thanks all. will post the RFC link when ready. :rocket:
